name: kvm_check_and_inject_events
prose: Precondition: vcpu is a valid vCPU and req_immediate_exit points to a writable bool. Postcondition: static function returning int. If is_guest_mode(vcpu) it first calls kvm_check_nested_events (otherwise r is 0). It then re-injects an event that is already marked injected: an injected exception via kvm_inject_exception, else (when no exception is pending) an injected NMI via the inject_nmi hook or an injected interrupt via the inject_irq hook. If r from the nested check was negative it jumps to the out label. Otherwise, if an exception is pending, it sets RF in RFLAGS for fault-class vectors, for #DB delivers the exception payload and clears DR7_GD, injects the exception, sets exception.pending false and exception.injected true. If vcpu->guest_debug has KVM_GUESTDBG_BLOCKIRQ set it then returns 0 immediately, skipping SMI, NMI and interrupt injection and the has_events check. Otherwise it handles a pending SMI (only when CONFIG_KVM_SMM), a pending NMI and an injectable interrupt, each through the vendor smi_allowed/nmi_allowed/interrupt_allowed hook, or -EBUSY when an earlier injection in this call already cleared can_inject; a negative result jumps to out, a positive result injects (enter_smm, inject_nmi, or queue plus inject_irq), a zero result leaves the event pending and enables the matching window. If the vCPU is in guest mode and the nested has_events hook reports events it sets *req_immediate_exit to true. It then returns 0. At out, a value of -EBUSY is turned into 0 with *req_immediate_exit set to true; any other negative value from kvm_check_nested_events or the allowed hooks is returned unchanged. *req_immediate_exit is written only on the has_events path and the -EBUSY conversion.
note: Checked x86.c:10244-10448. Round-15 reviewer claim that it never re-injects is WRONG (10283-10290 re-inject injected exception/NMI/IRQ). Earlier reviewer claim about missing BLOCKIRQ early return and success return was right and is covered (10359-10360, 10440). Slice cut the head (function starts 10244).

name: memslot_rmap_alloc
prose: Precondition: slot points to a memory slot whose arch.rmap[] entries are each NULL or a valid vmalloc-style array, and npages is the slot's page count. Postcondition: for each index i from 0 to KVM_NR_PAGE_SIZES-1 (level i+1) whose rmap entry is NULL it allocates a zeroed array of __kvm_mmu_slot_lpages(slot, npages, level) elements with __vcalloc(GFP_KERNEL_ACCOUNT); non-NULL entries are skipped untouched. If all entries are non-NULL after the loop it returns 0. If an allocation fails it calls memslot_rmap_free, which vfrees and sets to NULL every rmap entry of the slot, including entries that were already present on entry, and returns -ENOMEM. It takes no locks.
note: Checked x86.c:12647-12667 and memslot_rmap_free 12623-12631. Prior prose was correct; ENOMEM clause tightened (pre-existing arrays are also freed). Non-static function.

name: kvm_alloc_memslot_metadata
prose: Precondition: kvm is a valid VM and slot is a memory slot with npages, base_gfn and userspace_addr set. Postcondition: static function. It first zeroes slot->arch with memset. If kvm_memslots_have_rmaps(kvm) it calls memslot_rmap_alloc and returns that call's error (-ENOMEM) directly when it fails, in which case the callee has already freed the rmap arrays. For levels 2 through KVM_NR_PAGE_SIZES it allocates a zeroed lpage_info array with __vcalloc and stores it in slot->arch.lpage_info[level-2]; it sets disallow_lpage on entry 0 if base_gfn is not aligned to the level's page count, on the last entry if base_gfn+npages is not aligned, and on every entry of that level if base_gfn and (userspace_addr >> PAGE_SHIFT) differ in the low bits covered by that level. When CONFIG_KVM_GENERIC_MEMORY_ATTRIBUTES is set it calls kvm_mmu_init_memslot_memory_attributes (no return value used). It then calls kvm_page_track_create_memslot. It returns 0 if all steps succeed. If an lpage_info allocation or kvm_page_track_create_memslot fails it frees all rmap arrays and all lpage_info arrays (setting those pointers to NULL) and returns -ENOMEM, whatever nonzero value the page-track call produced. It takes no locks.
note: Checked x86.c:12669-12736. Prose from round 15 mostly right; rewritten to state the rmap-failure early return, the unconditional -ENOMEM for page-track failure and the CONFIG gating of the attributes call.

name: kvm_arch_prepare_memory_region
prose: Precondition: kvm is a valid VM, old and new are memory slots, and change is a kvm_mr_change value. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL if change is KVM_MR_MOVE and kvm_page_track_has_external_user(kvm) is true. If change is KVM_MR_CREATE or KVM_MR_MOVE it returns -EINVAL when new->base_gfn + new->npages - 1 is greater than kvm_mmu_max_gfn() or when kvm_is_gfn_alias() reports that last gfn is an alias; otherwise it returns the result of kvm_alloc_memslot_metadata(kvm, new), which is 0 on success or -ENOMEM with the new slot's arch metadata freed. If change is KVM_MR_FLAGS_ONLY it copies old->arch into new->arch with memcpy and returns 0. If change is KVM_MR_DELETE it touches no slot metadata and returns 0. For any other change value it emits a one-time warning (WARN_ON_ONCE) and returns -EIO. It takes no locks.
note: Checked x86.c:12754-12782. Prose of round 15 was accurate; reworded the CREATE/MOVE result (returns the callee result directly) and the DELETE case. Slice cut the head.

name: kvm_set_msr_common
prose: Precondition: vcpu is a valid vCPU and msr_info holds the MSR index, the data value and the host_initiated flag. Postcondition: if the index is the Xen hypercall page MSR (kvm_xen_is_hypercall_page_msr) and the write is not host-initiated, it returns the result of kvm_xen_write_hypercall_page without entering the switch. Otherwise it dispatches on the index. The following cases return the callee's result directly: set_efer (EFER), kvm_mtrr_set_msr (MTRR ranges and MTRRdefType), kvm_apic_set_base (APICBASE), kvm_x2apic_msr_write (x2APIC MSR range), set_msr_mce (MCG_CTL, MCG_STATUS and the MC bank ranges), kvm_hv_set_msr_common (Hyper-V MSR ranges, only when CONFIG_KVM_HYPERV is built), and kvm_pmu_set_msr (K7/P6 perf counter and event-select MSRs, and any unlisted MSR, when kvm_pmu_is_valid_msr accepts it). It returns KVM_MSR_RET_UNSUPPORTED for an unlisted MSR the PMU does not accept, for ARCH_CAPABILITIES or PERF_CAPABILITIES when the write is not host-initiated or the guest lacks the matching CPUID feature, for XSS when guest CPUID lacks XSAVES, and for the KVM paravirtual MSRs (wall clock, system time, async PF, async PF int and ack, steal time, PV EOI, poll control) when the guest lacks the matching KVM feature. It returns 1 for rejected writes, including: PERF_CAPABILITIES data bits outside kvm_caps.supported_perf_cap; PRED_CMD from the guest without the PRED_CMD capability, or data with reserved/unsupported IBPB/SBPB bits; FLUSH_CMD from the guest without FLUSH_L1D, with the host lacking FLUSH_L1D, or with data bits other than L1D_FLUSH; HWCR data that, after masking bits 0x40, 0x100 and 0x8, has bits outside bit 18 and bit 24; a nonzero FAM10H_MMIO_CONF_BASE; a PAT value failing kvm_pat_valid; MISC_ENABLE from the guest changing the PMU read-only bits, or changing the MWAIT bit without guest XMM3 when the NO_MWAIT quirk check allows that path; SMBASE when not host-initiated or CONFIG_KVM_SMM is off; XSS data outside guest_supported_xss; SMI_COUNT and PLATFORM_INFO when not host-initiated; STEAL_TIME when sched_info is off or reserved bits are set; POLL_CONTROL data with bits above bit 0; OSVW length or status without the OSVW feature; MISC_FEATURES_ENABLES with bits other than CPUID_FAULT, or CPUID_FAULT without supports_cpuid_fault; on 64-bit builds XFD and XFD_ERR from the guest without the XFD feature or with data outside kvm_guest_supported_xfd; and a nonzero return from kvm_pv_enable_async_pf, kvm_pv_enable_async_pf_int or kvm_lapic_set_pv_eoi. For the remaining listed MSRs the function stores or acts on the value and returns 0; this includes the silently ignored MSRs NB_CFG, UCODE_WRITE, VM_HSAVE_PA, PATCH_LOADER, BU_CFG2, DC_CFG, TW_CFG, EX_CFG and K7_CLK_CTL, BBL_CR_CTL3 (logged and dropped), a zero FAM10H_MMIO_CONF_BASE write, UCODE_REV when not host-initiated, and K7/P6 perf MSRs the PMU does not own. Accepted writes may update vCPU or VM state, refresh the PMU when perf_capabilities changes, execute wrmsr on the host PRED_CMD or FLUSH_CMD MSR for a nonzero value, adjust the TSC offset and request a clock update, write guest wall-clock or system-time memory, or complete async page faults. The function takes no lock itself.
note: Checked x86.c:3572-3964. Reviewer claims: round-15 XSS-data-outside-guest_supported_xss returns 1 is RIGHT (3766-3767); MWAIT return 1 also depends on the NO_MWAIT quirk check is RIGHT (3734-3737); round-2 HWCR claim is RIGHT as to masking of bits 0x40/0x100/0x8 first; round-1 original claim about Xen side effect right. Prose rewritten to enumerate cases. Slice cut the head.

name: kvm_arch_vcpu_ioctl
prose: Precondition: filp->private_data is a valid vCPU, ioctl is a KVM vCPU request code and arg is the raw argument (a user pointer for most requests, a scalar for KVM_SET_TSC_KHZ). Postcondition: x86 vCPU ioctl handler returning long. It calls vcpu_load(vcpu) before the switch and vcpu_put(vcpu) before returning, on both the out and out_nofree exits. At out it also kfrees the temporary buffer u.buffer (a NULL pointer, or the buffer allocated for LAPIC, XSAVE, XCRS or SREGS2 requests); the out_nofree exit is used only after memdup_user returned an error pointer, so that pointer is not freed. The returned value is: -EINVAL for an unrecognised ioctl; -EFAULT when a copy_from_user, copy_to_user, get_user or put_user step fails; -ENOMEM when a kzalloc fails; -EINVAL for state checks such as LAPIC requests without an in-kernel LAPIC, KVM_GET_XSAVE when guest_fpu.uabi_size exceeds sizeof(struct kvm_xsave), KVM_SET_TSC_KHZ with a protected TSC, a frequency at or above max_guest_tsc_khz when TSC control exists, or a failing kvm_set_tsc_khz, nested-state requests when nested ops are not enabled or the supplied header or flags are invalid, and SREGS2 requests on a vCPU with protected guest state; -E2BIG for KVM_GET_NESTED_STATE when the state size exceeds the caller's buffer size (after put_user stores the needed size, or -EFAULT if that put_user fails); -ENOTTY for KVM_MEMORY_ENCRYPT_OP when the vendor has no vcpu_mem_enc_ioctl hook; for KVM_GET_TSC_KHZ the vCPU's virtual_tsc_khz value; otherwise the value returned by the delegated helper, which is 0 on success for the copy-out requests. An SRCU read lock on kvm->srcu is taken and released around the msr_io, set-vapic-address and set-nested-state helpers, and kvm_vcpu_srcu_read_lock is taken around the set-vcpu-events helper.
note: Name fix: the packet name kvm_vcpu_ioctl is not defined in x86.c; the slice (5945-6197) lies inside kvm_arch_vcpu_ioctl (x86.c:5819-6296), slice cut the head. Checked every case and both exits. Prior prose missed -ENOTTY, KVM_GET_TSC_KHZ positive return and the buffer-free distinction.

name: kvm_vm_ioctl_enable_cap
prose: Precondition: kvm is a valid VM and cap points to a readable struct kvm_enable_cap. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL if cap->flags is nonzero or cap->cap is not one of the handled capabilities. For KVM_CAP_DISABLE_QUIRKS2 it returns -EINVAL when args[0] has bits outside kvm_caps.supported_quirks; this and KVM_CAP_DISABLE_QUIRKS then, under kvm->lock, OR args[0] masked to supported_quirks into kvm->arch.disabled_quirks and return 0. KVM_CAP_SPLIT_IRQCHIP, under kvm->lock, returns -EINVAL if args[0] exceeds MAX_NR_RESERVED_IOAPIC_PINS and -EEXIST if an in-kernel irqchip exists or vCPUs were already created; otherwise it sets split irqchip mode and the reserved pin count, clears the APICv absent inhibit and returns 0. KVM_CAP_X2APIC_API, without taking kvm->lock, returns -EINVAL for bits outside KVM_X2APIC_API_VALID_FLAGS, for both suppress-EOI-broadcast enable and disable bits set together, or for the enable bit without a split irqchip; otherwise it sets the requested x2apic fields and returns 0. KVM_CAP_X86_DISABLE_EXITS returns -EINVAL for bits outside kvm_get_allowed_disable_exits() and, under kvm->lock, leaves r at -EINVAL if vCPUs exist; otherwise it may log a one-time SMT-RSB warning, calls kvm_disable_exits and returns 0. KVM_CAP_MSR_PLATFORM_INFO, KVM_CAP_EXCEPTION_PAYLOAD and KVM_CAP_X86_TRIPLE_FAULT_EVENT store args[0] into kvm->arch without taking kvm->lock and return 0. KVM_CAP_X86_USER_SPACE_MSR returns -EINVAL for bits outside KVM_MSR_EXIT_REASON_VALID_MASK, else stores the mask and returns 0. KVM_CAP_X86_BUS_LOCK_EXIT returns -EINVAL for invalid mode bits or for OFF and EXIT both set; otherwise it enables bus_lock_detection_enabled only if kvm_caps.has_bus_lock_exit and the EXIT bit are set, and returns 0 either way. With CONFIG_X86_SGX_KVM, KVM_CAP_SGX_ATTRIBUTE returns the error from sgx_set_attribute, -EINVAL unless the allowed attributes are exactly PROVISIONKEY, else sets sgx_provisioning_allowed and returns 0. KVM_CAP_VM_COPY_ENC_CONTEXT_FROM and KVM_CAP_VM_MOVE_ENC_CONTEXT_FROM return -EINVAL if the vendor hook is absent, else the hook's result. KVM_CAP_EXIT_HYPERCALL returns -EINVAL for bits outside KVM_EXIT_HYPERCALL_VALID_MASK, else stores them and returns 0. KVM_CAP_EXIT_ON_EMULATION_FAILURE returns -EINVAL if args[0] has bits other than bit 0, else stores it and returns 0. KVM_CAP_PMU_CAPABILITY returns -EINVAL if enable_pmu is off or args[0] has bits outside KVM_CAP_PMU_VALID_MASK; under kvm->lock it sets enable_pmu and returns 0 only if no vCPUs exist, otherwise -EINVAL. KVM_CAP_MAX_VCPU_ID returns -EINVAL if args[0] exceeds KVM_MAX_VCPU_IDS; under kvm->lock it returns -EINVAL if bsp_vcpu_id is above args[0] or a different nonzero max_vcpu_ids is already set, 0 if the same value is already set, and otherwise stores it and returns 0. KVM_CAP_X86_NOTIFY_VMEXIT returns -EINVAL for invalid bits, when kvm_caps.has_notify_vmexit is false, or when the ENABLED bit is clear; under kvm->lock it stores the window and flags and returns 0 only if no vCPUs exist, otherwise -EINVAL. KVM_CAP_VM_DISABLE_NX_HUGE_PAGES returns -EPERM without CAP_SYS_BOOT, -EINVAL if args[0] is nonzero, and under kvm->lock sets disable_nx_huge_pages and returns 0 only if no vCPUs exist, otherwise -EINVAL. KVM_CAP_X86_APIC_BUS_CYCLES_NS returns -EINVAL if args[0] is zero or (U32_MAX*128) times it overflows u64; under kvm->lock it returns -ENXIO without an in-kernel irqchip, -EINVAL if vCPUs exist, otherwise stores the bus cycle ns and returns 0. kvm->lock is taken and released within the cases that take it; no memory or reference is left for the caller.
note: Checked x86.c:6353-6623. Reviewer round-15 claim (X2APIC_API, MSR_PLATFORM_INFO, EXCEPTION_PAYLOAD, TRIPLE_FAULT_EVENT modify kvm->arch without kvm->lock) is RIGHT (6394-6418, 6442-6453); old prose lock sentence was too broad. Round-2 -EEXIST claim right (6379-6383). Round-1 claim right. Slice starts mid function (head at 6353).

name: kvm_arch_vm_ioctl
prose: Precondition: filp->private_data is a valid VM, ioctl is a VM request code and arg is the raw argument (a user pointer for most requests, a scalar for KVM_SET_BOOT_CPU_ID and KVM_SET_TSC_KHZ). Postcondition: x86 VM ioctl handler returning int, initial value -ENOTTY. An unrecognised ioctl returns -ENOTTY. The in-kernel PIC/IOAPIC/PIT requests exist only when CONFIG_KVM_IOAPIC is set, the Xen requests only with CONFIG_KVM_XEN, KVM_HYPERV_EVENTFD only with CONFIG_KVM_HYPERV. Failures of copy_from_user, copy_to_user or memdup_user return -EFAULT (or the memdup_user error pointer's errno); KVM_X86_SET_MSR_FILTER returns -EFAULT directly on a failed copy. Request-specific results: KVM_CREATE_IRQCHIP, under kvm->lock, returns -EEXIST if an irqchip exists, -ENOTTY if the VM has protected EOIs, -EINVAL if vCPUs exist, otherwise the error from PIC, IOAPIC or default routing setup (tearing down what it created) or 0 on success. KVM_CREATE_PIT and KVM_CREATE_PIT2, under kvm->lock, return -EEXIST if a PIT exists, -ENOENT without an in-kernel PIC, -ENOMEM if kvm_create_pit fails, else 0. KVM_GET_IRQCHIP and KVM_SET_IRQCHIP return -ENXIO without a full irqchip, else the helper result (GET also copies out), and free the memdup_user buffer. KVM_GET_PIT, KVM_GET_PIT2, KVM_SET_PIT, KVM_SET_PIT2 and KVM_REINJECT_CONTROL return -ENXIO without a PIT; the SET variants hold kvm->lock around the helper. KVM_SET_IDENTITY_MAP_ADDR holds kvm->lock and returns -EINVAL if vCPUs exist. KVM_SET_BOOT_CPU_ID, under kvm->lock, returns -EBUSY if vCPUs exist, -EINVAL if arg exceeds KVM_MAX_VCPU_IDS or a set max_vcpu_ids, else stores the bsp id and returns 0. KVM_SET_TSC_KHZ returns -EINVAL if TSC control exists and the value is at or above max_guest_tsc_khz, uses the host tsc_khz for a zero value, and under kvm->lock stores default_tsc_khz and returns 0 only if no vCPUs exist, otherwise -EINVAL. KVM_GET_TSC_KHZ returns kvm->arch.default_tsc_khz. KVM_MEMORY_ENCRYPT_OP and the register and unregister region requests return -ENOTTY if the vendor hook is missing, else the hook's result. The remaining requests (TSS address, nr mmu pages, Xen, clock, Hyper-V eventfd, PMU event filter, MSR filter) return the delegated helper's result.
note: Name fix: packet name kvm_vm_ioctl is not defined in x86.c; the slice (6986-7238) lies in kvm_arch_vm_ioctl (x86.c:6873-7237), slice cut the head. Old prose lock list was incomplete (omitted KVM_SET_IDENTITY_MAP_ADDR, KVM_CREATE_IRQCHIP, KVM_CREATE_PIT*), and it said the KVM_SET_TSC_KHZ -EINVAL was only out-of-range; kept both causes here.

name: x86_emulate_instruction
prose: Precondition: vcpu is a valid vCPU with an emulator context; insn and insn_len either are NULL/0 or describe the instruction bytes; cr2_or_gpa is the faulting address when EMULTYPE_PF is set. Postcondition: it first clears EMULTYPE_ALLOW_RETRY_PF (with a WARN_ON_ONCE) if the vCPU is in guest mode or EMULTYPE_PF is not set. It then calls kvm_check_emulate_insn; if that result is not X86EMUL_CONTINUE it returns 1 for X86EMUL_RETRY_INSTR or X86EMUL_PROPAGATE_FAULT, returns 1 if kvm_unprotect_and_retry_on_failure succeeds, returns 0 after kvm_prepare_event_vectoring_exit for X86EMUL_UNHANDLEABLE_VECTORING, and otherwise returns handle_emulation_failure(). After a successful check it sets l1tf_flush_l1d; unless EMULTYPE_NO_DECODE is set it clears the exception queue, returns the value stored by kvm_vcpu_check_code_breakpoint when that reports a code breakpoint, and decodes the instruction; on decode failure it queues #UD and returns 1 for EMULTYPE_TRAP_UD or EMULTYPE_TRAP_UD_FORCED, returns 1 after an unprotect-and-retry, returns 1 after injecting a pending emulator exception when EMULTYPE_SKIP is not set, and otherwise returns handle_emulation_failure(). With EMULTYPE_VMWARE_GP set and a non-backdoor opcode it queues #GP(0) and returns 1. With EMULTYPE_SKIP it returns 0 if EMULTYPE_SKIP_SOFT_INT is set and the instruction is not a soft interrupt; with EMULTYPE_COMPLETE_USER_EXIT it goes to writeback with r equal to 1; otherwise it writes RIP, clears RF in RFLAGS if the emulator flags had it, and returns 1. If EMULTYPE_ALLOW_RETRY_PF remains set and the instruction is not a page-table-writing one it returns 1 when kvm_mmu_unprotect_gfn_and_retry succeeds. Otherwise it runs x86_emulate_insn: EMULATION_INTERCEPTED returns 1; EMULATION_FAILED returns 1 after a successful unprotect-and-retry, else handle_emulation_failure(). Otherwise r becomes 1 after injecting a pending exception (and mmio_needed cleared); 0 for pending PIO (pio-out clears pio.count; pio-in sets complete_userspace_io and suppresses writeback), for MMIO (counting an MMIO exit, suppressing writeback for reads) and for an already-set complete_userspace_io; EMULATION_RESTART restarts emulation; else 1. On writeback it toggles interruptibility, clears emulate_regs_need_sync_to_vcpu, and only if there is no exception or a trap-like exception it records PMU retired events, writes RIP, replaces r with kvm_vcpu_do_singlestep() when r is nonzero and TF or single-step guest debug is active, calls update_emulated_instruction and writes RFLAGS; a fault-like pending exception skips RIP and RFLAGS writes. It requests KVM_REQ_EVENT if IF was newly set. Without writeback it sets emulate_regs_need_sync_to_vcpu to true. It returns r, which is 0 or 1 from the paths above.
note: Checked x86.c:9024-9244. Reviewer claims all RIGHT: round-15 omits return 1 for RETRY_INSTR/PROPAGATE_FAULT (9038-9039); round-2 pio-out returns 0 and WARN-clear (9031-9034, 9185-9193); round-1 fault-like exception skips RIP/EFLAGS writeback (9220-9230). Prose rewritten with full return list. Slice cut the head.

name: kvm_xen_vcpu_set_attr
prose: Precondition: vcpu is a valid vCPU and data points to a kvm_xen_vcpu_attr; the caller holds neither kvm->arch.xen.xen_lock nor the kvm->srcu read lock. Postcondition: the function takes xen_lock and the SRCU read lock on entry, switches on data->type, and releases both locks before the single return, so it returns with neither held. The result starts as -ENOENT for an unrecognised type. VCPU_INFO (gpa) and VCPU_INFO_HVA deactivate the vcpu_info cache and return 0 for KVM_XEN_INVALID_GPA or a zero hva, else return the error of kvm_gpc_activate or kvm_gpc_activate_hva and, on success, request KVM_REQ_CLOCK_UPDATE. VCPU_TIME_INFO behaves the same for the time-info cache. RUNSTATE_ADDR returns -EOPNOTSUPP if sched_info_on() is false; for KVM_XEN_INVALID_GPA it deactivates both runstate caches and returns 0; otherwise it activates the first (and, when the structure crosses a page, the second) runstate cache, deactivating both and returning the error if either activation fails, and on success calls kvm_xen_update_runstate_guest and returns 0. RUNSTATE_CURRENT returns -EOPNOTSUPP without sched_info, -EINVAL if the state is above RUNSTATE_offline, else updates the runstate and returns 0. RUNSTATE_DATA returns -EOPNOTSUPP without sched_info, -EINVAL if the state is above RUNSTATE_offline, if state_entry_time differs from the sum of the four times, or if get_kvmclock_ns is below state_entry_time; otherwise it stores the state, entry time and times and returns 0. RUNSTATE_ADJUST returns -EOPNOTSUPP without sched_info, -EINVAL if the state is above RUNSTATE_offline and not (u64)-1, if state_entry_time differs from the sum of the four times, or if get_kvmclock_ns is below the existing entry time plus the adjustment; otherwise it adds the adjustments, updates the runstate (or the guest copy if the state is -1 and the runstate cache is active) and returns 0. VCPU_ID returns -EINVAL for a value of KVM_MAX_VCPUS or more, else stores it. TIMER returns -EINVAL if the port is nonzero and the priority is not KVM_IRQ_ROUTING_XEN_EVTCHN_PRIO_2LEVEL; otherwise it stops the timer, stores the port as timer_virq, starts the timer if port and expires_ns are both nonzero, and returns 0. UPCALL_VECTOR returns -EINVAL for a vector from 1 to 0xf, else stores it and returns 0.
note: Checked xen.c:906-1148. Reviewer round-15 claim RIGHT: RUNSTATE_ADJUST allows state == (u64)-1 (1065-1069); prose now says CURRENT/DATA/ADJUST separately. Old claim that every runstate attribute errors with -EOPNOTSUPP without sched_info is true for RUNSTATE_ADDR/CURRENT/DATA/ADJUST and is kept as such. Slice (1022-1275) starts mid function; the function head is at 906.

name: kvm_xen_schedop_poll
prose: Precondition: vcpu is a valid vCPU, longmode says whether the guest uses the 64-bit sched_poll layout, param is a guest virtual address of a sched_poll structure, and r points to a writable u64. Postcondition: it returns false without writing *r if the vCPU has no in-kernel LAPIC or the VM's Xen hvm_config flags lack KVM_XEN_HVM_CONFIG_EVTCHN_SEND. Otherwise it returns true. It reads the structure from guest memory (a 16-byte compat structure when CONFIG_64BIT and not longmode); a read failure sets *r to -EFAULT and returns true. If nr_ports exceeds 128 it sets *r to -EINVAL and returns true; for nr_ports above 1 it kmallocs a ports array and sets *r to -ENOMEM and returns true if that fails; those three early returns do not touch poll_mask. It then reads the ports array from guest memory; a read failure sets *r to -EFAULT, and a port at or above max_evtchn_port(kvm) sets *r to -EINVAL; both go to the out label. Otherwise it sets poll_evtchn to the single port (or -1 when nr_ports is not 1) and sets the vCPU's bit in poll_mask. If wait_pending_event finds no pending polled event it sets the vCPU to KVM_MP_STATE_HALTED, arms the poll timer if the timeout is nonzero, calls kvm_vcpu_halt, deletes the timer if one was armed, and sets the state back to KVM_MP_STATE_RUNNABLE. It then sets poll_evtchn to 0 and *r to 0. At out it clears the vCPU's poll_mask bit and, when nr_ports is above 1, kfrees the ports array, then returns true.
note: Checked xen.c:1471-1570. Reviewer claims all RIGHT: precondition said ports are readable/valid but code reads and validates them (1526-1537); -ENOMEM path (1519-1522); early returns do not clear poll_mask (1489-1522 vs out at 1563-1565). Precondition rewritten. Slice (1532-1782) starts after the head; function head at 1471.

name: poly_cos
prose: Precondition: st0_ptr points to a valid FPU_REG holding the already range-reduced argument whose magnitude is at most pi/4 (exponent at most 0, and when the exponent is 0 the significand is at most 0xc90fdaa22168c234); the sign is not examined. Postcondition: void function. When PARANOID is defined and the argument is out of that range it raises EXCEPTION(EX_Invalid), copies CONST_QNaN to register 0 with TAG_Special and returns without computing. In the normal path it computes cos of the argument with extended-precision fixed-point polynomial arithmetic. If the argument exponent is below -1, or is -1 with sigh at or below 0xb00d6f54, it uses the direct polynomial; if the resulting accumulator.msw is 0 it copies CONST_1 to register 0 with TAG_Valid and returns. Otherwise (and in the other branch, which works from pi/2 minus the argument with a fix-up term) it builds a positive result with the computed exponent and significand and copies it to register 0 with FPU_copy_to_reg0 and TAG_Valid. When PARANOID is defined and the stored result has a non-negative exponent and a significand above 0x8000000000000000, it then raises EXCEPTION(EX_INTERNAL | 0x151). It acquires no locks and reads only constant coefficient tables besides its argument.
note: Checked poly_sin.c:201-379. Reviewer round-15 claim that the PARANOID early return is not present is WRONG: it is at poly_sin.c:208-216 inside #ifdef PARANOID (head cut out of the packet slice 254-379). Old precondition said non-negative: sign is not checked, removed. Name outside slice.

name: do_kern_addr_fault
prose: Precondition: address is in the kernel part of the address space, hw_error_code is the hardware page-fault error code for the fault, regs describes the faulting context. Postcondition: void function. It first emits WARN_ON_ONCE if hw_error_code has X86_PF_PK set (and continues). On CONFIG_X86_32, if none of X86_PF_RSVD, X86_PF_USER and X86_PF_PROT is set in hw_error_code it calls vmalloc_fault(address) and returns if that returns a value of 0 or more; vmalloc_fault can copy entries from the reference page table into the current one, so page tables may be modified on that path. It then returns if is_f00f_bug(regs, hw_error_code, address) is true, returns if spurious_kernel_fault(hw_error_code, address) returns nonzero, and returns if kprobe_page_fault(regs, X86_TRAP_PF) returns true (this case also triggers WARN_ON_ONCE). If none of those returned, it calls bad_area_nosemaphore(regs, hw_error_code, address) and then returns. It does not take mmap_lock.
note: Checked fault.c:1134-1195. Reviewer round-15 claims RIGHT: WARN_ON_ONCE does not end the function (1142) and vmalloc_fault can modify page tables on x86_32 (1169-1172); old prose said it never modified page tables. Round-1 CONFIG_X86_32 vmalloc path covered. Slice cut the head.

name: arch_memremap_can_ram_remap
prose: Precondition: none; any physical address, size and MEMREMAP_* flags may be passed. Postcondition: returns true if cc_platform_has(CC_ATTR_MEM_ENCRYPT) is false; otherwise returns true if flags has MEMREMAP_ENC; otherwise returns false if flags has MEMREMAP_DEC; otherwise, if cc_platform_has(CC_ATTR_HOST_MEM_ENCRYPT) is true and the address is setup data (memremap_is_setup_data) or EFI data (memremap_is_efi_data), returns false; in the remaining cases it returns the negation of memremap_should_map_decrypted(phys_addr, size), regardless of the host-memory-encryption attribute. It writes nothing and takes no locks.
note: Checked ioremap.c:729-748. Reviewer round-15 claim RIGHT: old prose omitted true when host encryption is active, the range is neither setup data nor EFI data and memremap_should_map_decrypted is false (747). Return order: ENC is tested before DEC.

name: populate_pud
prose: Precondition: cpa describes a mapping of cpa->numpages pages starting at address start with cpa->pfn as the first pfn, p4d points to a valid P4D entry, and pgprot is the protection to apply. Postcondition: static function returning int. If start is not 1G aligned it maps the pages up to the next 1G boundary or the end of the range through populate_pmd; it returns -1 if allocating a PMD page fails and returns populate_pmd's negative value (which is -1) if that call fails. It returns the page count if that leading part covered all cpa->numpages pages. It then maps whole 1G-aligned runs with 1G pages when the CPU has X86_FEATURE_GBPAGES, advancing cpa->pfn and the page count. For any remaining trailing range it allocates a PMD page if needed (returning -1 on failure) and calls populate_pmd; if that call returns a negative value the function does not propagate it but returns the count of pages mapped before the trailing part; otherwise it adds the trailing pages to the count. The normal return value is the number of pages mapped, equal to cpa->numpages when everything was populated.
note: Checked set_memory.c:1683-1759 and populate_pmd 1609-1681. Reviewer round-15 claims RIGHT: trailing populate_pmd failure returns cur_pages (1753-1754), and populate_pmd's -1 can come from PTE or PMD page allocation (1633-1634, 1655-1656, 1674-1675), so -1 is not only a PMD allocation failure.

name: pti_clone_pgtable
prose: Precondition: start and end bound a kernel virtual range, level is a pti_clone_level and late_text selects how a large user PMD found during a PTE-level walk is treated. Postcondition: void function. It loops addr from start while addr < end, stopping if addr wraps below start. For each address it returns (after WARN_ON) if the kernel PGD or P4D entry is none. A none PUD skips to the next PUD boundary (WARN_ON_ONCE if addr was not PUD aligned) and a none PMD skips to the next PMD boundary (WARN_ON_ONCE if not PMD aligned). For a PMD that is a leaf, or when level is PTI_CLONE_PMD, it obtains the user page table PMD with pti_user_pagetable_walk_pmd, returns after WARN_ON if that is NULL or the source PMD lacks _PAGE_PRESENT, sets _PAGE_GLOBAL on the source PMD when the CPU has PGE, copies the PMD to the user page table and advances to the next PMD boundary. Otherwise, when level is PTI_CLONE_PTE, it advances one page past a none PTE, returns after WARN_ON if the source PTE is not present, obtains the user PTE with pti_user_pagetable_walk_pte(addr, late_text) and returns after WARN_ON if that is NULL, sets _PAGE_GLOBAL on the source PTE when the CPU has PGE, copies the PTE and advances one page. If a present non-leaf PMD is reached with a level other than PTI_CLONE_PMD or PTI_CLONE_PTE it calls BUG(). An early return leaves the rest of the range uncloned; page-table pages allocated by the walk helpers remain attached to the user page table. The user-side walkers return NULL for allocation failure, for a large user PUD, for a user PTE already marked _PAGE_USER, and for a large user PMD when late_text is false; with late_text true a large user PMD is cleared instead.
note: Checked pti.c:320-427 and the pti_user_pagetable_walk_pmd/pte helpers (211-291). Old prose mostly right; BUG precondition corrected (BUG only for a present non-leaf PMD with an unsupported level). Slice cut the head.

name: pti_clone_entry_text
prose: Precondition: the entry text range [__entry_text_start, __entry_text_end) is mapped in the kernel page tables. Postcondition: static void function that calls pti_clone_pgtable(__entry_text_start, __entry_text_end, PTI_LEVEL_KERNEL_IMAGE, late) and returns. The cloning behaviour is that of pti_clone_pgtable: present entry-text PMDs or PTEs are copied into the user page table (with _PAGE_GLOBAL set on source and copy when the CPU has PGE), and a large user PMD met during a PTE-level walk is cleared when late is true and causes an early return with a warning when late is false; an early return from pti_clone_pgtable leaves the rest of the range uncloned.
note: Checked pti.c:512-517. Prose kept in substance; the late=false behaviour made explicit.

name: allocate_global_asid
prose: Precondition: the caller holds global_asid_lock (checked with lockdep_assert_held). Postcondition: static function returning u16. If last_global_asid is at least MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE - 1 it first calls reset_global_asid_space, which issues invlpgb_flush_all_nonglobals, clears from global_asid_used the bits set in global_asid_freed, clears global_asid_freed and sets last_global_asid to TLB_NR_DYN_ASIDS. It then finds the first zero bit of global_asid_used at or after last_global_asid below MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE. If the result is at least MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE and global_asid_available is zero it issues a one-time VM_WARN_ONCE and returns 0; no global ASID is claimed in that case, but the reset described above may already have been performed. Otherwise it sets that bit in global_asid_used, sets last_global_asid to it, decrements global_asid_available by one and returns it. If no zero bit was found but global_asid_available is nonzero, the position is MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE, so the bit set is one past the end of the bitmap and that value is returned. The lock stays held on return.
note: Checked tlb.c:316-340 and reset_global_asid_space 298-314. Reviewer round-15 claim RIGHT: the failure path can follow a reset, so state is not unchanged (323-333). Round-2 out-of-bounds claim is also right (326-338).

name: do_jit
prose: Precondition: bpf_prog->insnsi holds bpf_prog->len valid BPF instructions, addrs has room for len + 1 entries, image and rw_image (when non-NULL) are large enough for oldproglen bytes, and bpf_prog->aux->extable (when non-NULL) has num_exentries slots. Postcondition: static function. It emits the x86-64 prologue and then the translation of each BPF instruction into a temporary buffer, copying each chunk into rw_image when image is non-NULL, and records the running byte offsets in addrs[0..len]. It returns the total generated length proglen on success. For PROBE_MEM loads (BPF_PROBE_MEM and PROBE_MEMSX) it also emits a kernel-address range check and, when an extable exists, fills the next exception-table entry with the delta, EX_TYPE_BPF, the instruction length and the destination register so a faulting load zeroes that register. For PROBE_MEM32 loads and PROBE_ATOMIC load-acquire accesses the entry records the arena register and the destination register to clear; for PROBE_MEM32 stores, PROBE_MEM32 ST and PROBE_ATOMIC stores the entry records the arena register but uses DONT_CLEAR, so a faulting store does not zero any register. It returns a negative value instead of a length: -EFAULT for an extable counter overflow, an extable delta that does not fit in 32 bits (checked only in the PROBE_MEM path), a destination register above BPF_REG_9, an unsupported 1- or 2-byte atomic RMW, a jump offset out of range, an instruction longer than BPF_MAX_INSN_SIZE, an image overflow or addrs mismatch on the final pass, or an unpopulated extable; -EINVAL for a call with a zero immediate, a failed emit_call or spectre-BHB barrier, or an unknown opcode; or the error returned by an atomic emit helper. A negative return leaves no usable program.
note: Checked bpf_jit_comp.c:1622-2761 (extable code 2117-2318, return list via grep). Reviewer round-15 claim RIGHT: PROBE_MEM32 stores set fixup_reg = DONT_CLEAR (2187-2190). Old prose said every probed access clears the destination register. Name was outside slice (head at 1622).

name: get_cond_jmp_opcode
prose: Precondition: none; op is a BPF jump opcode byte and is_cmp_lo says whether the compare is on the low 32-bit halves. Postcondition: static pure function that maps op to an ia32 conditional-jump opcode byte: BPF_JEQ (0x10) gives 0x74; BPF_JSET (0x40) and BPF_JNE (0x50) give 0x75; BPF_JGT (0x20) gives 0x77; BPF_JLT (0xA0) gives 0x72; BPF_JGE (0x30) gives 0x73; BPF_JLE (0xB0) gives 0x76; BPF_JSGT (0x60) gives 0x7F when is_cmp_lo is false and 0x77 when true; BPF_JSLT (0xC0) gives 0x7C or 0x72; BPF_JSGE (0x70) gives 0x7D or 0x73; BPF_JSLE (0xD0) gives 0x7E or 0x76. Any other op value gives COND_JMP_OPCODE_INVALID (0xFF). It reads no memory and takes no locks.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (op == 0x10 ? result == 0x74 : (op == 0x40 || op == 0x50) ? result == 0x75 : op == 0x20 ? result == 0x77 : op == 0xA0 ? result == 0x72 : op == 0x30 ? result == 0x73 : op == 0xB0 ? result == 0x76 : op == 0x60 ? result == (is_cmp_lo ? 0x77 : 0x7F) : op == 0xC0 ? result == (is_cmp_lo ? 0x72 : 0x7C) : op == 0x70 ? result == (is_cmp_lo ? 0x73 : 0x7D) : op == 0xD0 ? result == (is_cmp_lo ? 0x76 : 0x7E) : result == 0xFF); */
note: Checked bpf_jit_comp32.c:1422-1489 and the IA32_J* defines (110-119), COND_JMP_OPCODE_INVALID = 0xFF (121). Old prose (eleven opcodes) was correct. Contract rewritten as a total function including the 0xFF default, answering the round-15 reviewer claim (RIGHT: old contract required op in the handled set and omitted the default).

name: pci_conf1_write
prose: Precondition: none; the function validates its own arguments. Postcondition: static function returning int. If seg is nonzero, or bus is above 255, or devfn is above 255, or reg is above 4095, it returns -EINVAL without taking pci_config_lock and without touching any port. Otherwise it takes pci_config_lock with interrupts disabled, writes the type-1 configuration address (0x80000000 with the extended register bits, bus, devfn and reg & 0xFC) to port 0xCF8, and for len 1, 2 or 4 writes the low byte, low 16 bits or the full 32 bits of value to port 0xCFC plus (reg & 3), plus (reg & 2) or plus 0 respectively; for any other len it writes nothing to the data port. It then releases the lock, restores the interrupt state and returns 0.
note: Checked direct.c:52-79. Prose was right; contract left empty because the function touches the global lock and I/O ports.

name: pci_conf2_write
prose: Precondition: none; a nonzero seg only triggers WARN_ON and is otherwise ignored. Postcondition: static function returning int. If bus is above 255, or devfn is above 255, or reg is above 255 it returns -EINVAL without taking the lock or writing any port. If bit 0x10 of the device number (devfn >> 3 masked to 5 bits) is set it returns PCIBIOS_DEVICE_NOT_FOUND (0x86) without taking the lock or writing a port. Otherwise it takes pci_config_lock with interrupts disabled, writes 0xF0 | ((devfn & 7) << 1) to port 0xCF8 and the bus to port 0xCFA, and for len 1, 2 or 4 writes the low byte, low 16 bits or full 32 bits of value to port (0xC000 | (dev << 8) | reg); for any other len it writes nothing to the data port. It then writes 0 to port 0xCF8, releases the lock, restores the interrupt state and returns 0.
note: Checked direct.c:137-175. Prose was right; added the data-port address. Contract left empty because the function touches the lock and I/O ports.

name: pci_xen_init
prose: Precondition: none; it is called during init and tests the Xen domain type itself. Postcondition: it returns -ENODEV (-19) without further effects if the kernel is not a Xen PV domain or is the initial domain. Otherwise it prints an informational message, calls pcibios_set_cache_line_size, sets pcibios_enable_irq to xen_pcifront_enable_irq and pcibios_disable_irq to NULL, calls acpi_noirq_set, calls xen_setup_pci_msi (which installs the Xen MSI setup and teardown callbacks and replaces x86_init.irqs.create_pci_msi_domain with xen_create_pci_msi_domain) and returns 0.
note: Checked xen.c:494-511 and xen_setup_pci_msi 467-488. Prose right, contract dropped because the function sets global hooks. Note xen_setup_pci_msi can warn and return early for a non-PV, non-HVM domain.

name: EFI_ATTR_SHOW(name)
prose: Macro definition that generates a static ssize_t sysfs show function name_show(struct kobject *kobj, struct kobj_attribute *attr, char *buf). It is invoked for fw_vendor, runtime and config_table, producing fw_vendor_show, runtime_show and config_table_show. Each generated function formats the corresponding unsigned long variable efi_fw_vendor, efi_runtime or efi_config_table into buf as "0x%lx\n" with sprintf and returns sprintf's character count; kobj and attr are unused and buf is assumed large enough. It takes no locks and retains no reference.
note: Checked efi.c:891-902. Name uses the macro definition head because the three functions are macro-generated.

name: imr_add_range
prose: Precondition: none; callers pass a physical base and size (both 1 KiB aligned, size nonzero) and read/write masks. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV (with a one-time warning) if the IMR driver is not initialised, before taking the lock. Otherwise it returns the error of imr_check_params (-EINVAL) if base or size is unaligned to 1 KiB or size is zero, and -ENOTSUPP if the range with the given masks would read as a disabled IMR; these also occur before the lock is taken. It then takes imr_dev's mutex and scans all max_imr IMRs; it returns the error of a failed imr_read, or -EINVAL if an enabled IMR contains base or end (an enabled IMR lying wholly inside the new range is not detected); the last disabled IMR slot found is the one used, and if none is found it returns -ENOMEM. It then writes the IMR for the range base to base + size - IMR_ALIGN with the given masks and returns imr_write's result (0 on success); if imr_write fails it attempts to write a disabled IMR into the slot, ignoring that second result, and returns the original error. The mutex is released on every path after it is taken.
note: Checked imr.c:298-388. Old prose accurate; precondition rewritten because -ENODEV and parameter errors are returned by the function, and the overlap-test limitation noted.

name: __imr_remove_range
prose: Precondition: none; reg selects the IMR by index when it is 0 or more, equals -1 to select by address range, and for a value below -1 the base and size are used for the search without validation. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV (with a one-time warning) if the driver is not initialised. If reg is -1 it returns the error of imr_check_params (-EINVAL) when base or size is unaligned or size is zero. It then takes imr_dev's mutex. For reg of 0 or more it reads that IMR (returning imr_read's error on failure) and returns -ENODEV if the IMR is disabled or has IMR_LOCK set in addr_lo; base and size are not used for matching. For a negative reg it scans the IMRs for the first that is enabled, not locked, and whose addr_lo and addr_hi, converted to physical, equal base and base + size - IMR_ALIGN, returning imr_read's error on a read failure and -ENODEV if none matches. For the selected IMR it writes a disabled IMR (zero addresses and all-access masks) and returns imr_write's result, 0 on success; on a write failure no rollback is done. The mutex is released on every path after it is taken.
note: Checked imr.c:407-484. Old prose right except the parenthetical claiming imr_read fails for out-of-range reg, which the code does not state; removed. Lock bit is tested on addr_lo (442, 454).

name: imr_remove_range
prose: Precondition: none; base and size should be 1 KiB aligned with a nonzero size. Postcondition: exported function that returns __imr_remove_range(-1, base, size). That call returns -ENODEV (with a one-time warning) if the IMR driver is not initialised; -EINVAL from imr_check_params if base or size is unaligned or size is zero; under imr_dev's mutex, imr_read's error if reading an IMR fails; -ENODEV if no enabled, unlocked IMR has physical addr_lo equal to base and physical addr_hi equal to base + size - IMR_ALIGN; and otherwise it overwrites the first such IMR with a disabled IMR and returns imr_write's result (0 on success, with no rollback on failure). The mutex is released on every path after it is taken.
note: Checked imr.c:499-502 with __imr_remove_range 407-484. Prose kept, wording tightened.

name: imr_clear
prose: Precondition: none; reg is the IMR index. Postcondition: static inline function that returns __imr_remove_range(reg, 0, 0). For reg of 0 or more it takes imr_dev's mutex, reads IMR reg (returning imr_read's error on failure), returns -ENODEV if it is disabled or has IMR_LOCK set in addr_lo, and otherwise overwrites it with a disabled IMR and returns imr_write's result (0 on success, with no rollback on failure); imr_check_params is not called for these values. If the driver is not initialised it returns -ENODEV with a one-time warning. If reg is -1 it returns -EINVAL because imr_check_params rejects size 0. For a reg below -1 it searches for the first enabled, unlocked IMR whose physical addr_lo is 0 and whose physical addr_hi equals the wrapped value 0 - IMR_ALIGN, returns -ENODEV if none matches, and otherwise clears it as above. The mutex is released on every path after it is taken.
note: Checked imr.c:518-521 with __imr_remove_range. Round-1 reviewer claim that imr_check_params is not called for reg >= 0 is RIGHT (424-428); prose already stated that and now states the reg == -1 case separately.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(arch_prctl, int, option, unsigned long, arg2)
prose: Precondition: option and arg2 are the raw syscall arguments (option is an int selector, arg2 an unsigned long treated as a user pointer). Postcondition: the generated syscall function for arch_prctl simply returns arch_prctl(current, option, (unsigned long __user *)arg2). In that function: option ARCH_SET_FS or ARCH_SET_GS stores the arg2 value, unchecked, as the FS or GS base in current->thread.regs.regs.gp and the result is 0; option ARCH_GET_FS or ARCH_GET_GS writes the stored base to the user address arg2 with put_user and the result is 0 on success or -EFAULT if that write fails; any other option gives -EINVAL. It acquires no locks or references.
note: Checked syscalls_64.c:16-46. The slice contains the UML arch_prctl function and this SYSCALL_DEFINE2 wrapper; the exact generated symbol name depends on syscall-wrapper configuration so it is not named. Contract dropped (it reads and writes task state and user memory).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE6(mmap, unsigned long, addr, unsigned long, len, unsigned long, prot, unsigned long, flags, unsigned long, fd, unsigned long, off)
prose: Precondition: addr, len, prot, flags, fd and off are the six unsigned long syscall arguments. Postcondition: the generated syscall function for mmap returns -EINVAL, without calling anything else, if off has any bit set below PAGE_SIZE (off & ~PAGE_MASK is nonzero). Otherwise it returns the value of ksys_mmap_pgoff(addr, len, prot, flags, fd, off >> PAGE_SHIFT), which is a mapped address or a negative errno as produced by that callee. It acquires no locks or references itself.
note: Checked syscalls_64.c:56-64. Old prose said off >> 12; the code shifts by PAGE_SHIFT. Generated symbol name depends on syscall-wrapper configuration so it is not named.

name: psmash
prose: Precondition: pfn is a page frame number intended for an SNP PSMASH of the 2 MB page at pfn << PAGE_SHIFT. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV if cc_platform_has(CC_ATTR_HOST_SEV_SNP) is false, then -EINVAL if pfn_valid(pfn) is false. Otherwise it executes the PSMASH instruction on pfn << PAGE_SHIFT (byte sequence F3 0F 01 FF with the address in rax) and returns the value the instruction leaves in eax as an int, which is the instruction's status code (0 for success; nonzero values are the SNP firmware status codes). It acquires no locks or references.
note: Checked sev.c:863-881. Reviewer claims: round-1/2 mechanical complaints about contract wrong; contract dropped (function reads global platform state and executes an instruction). Positive firmware error codes are not stated in this function; softened.

name: adjust_direct_map
prose: Precondition: pfn is a page frame number in the direct map and rmp_level is a page level for an RMP entry. Postcondition: static function returning int. It returns -EINVAL (after WARN_ON_ONCE) if rmp_level is greater than PG_LEVEL_2M, -EINVAL if pfn_valid(pfn) is false, and -EINVAL if rmp_level is PG_LEVEL_2M and pfn is not 2 MB aligned or pfn + PTRS_PER_PMD - 1 is not valid. If rmp_level is PG_LEVEL_2M it returns 0 without changing the mapping. Otherwise it looks up the direct-map entry for the pfn's kernel address; if there is no entry, it is none, or it is already at 4K level it returns 0 without change. Otherwise it calls set_memory_4k on that address for page_level_size(rmp_level) / PAGE_SIZE pages, prints a warning if it returns nonzero, and returns its result. It acquires no locks or references itself.
note: Checked sev.c:910-957. Reviewer claims: round-1 (2M level returns 0 without splitting) RIGHT (940-941); round-2 (code returns -EINVAL for rmp_level > PG_LEVEL_2M) RIGHT (924-925); round-15 (specific results needed) addressed. Contract dropped because the function consults the page tables and has global side effects.

name: mc_debug_enable
prose: Precondition: runs as an early initcall after boot-parameter parsing has set mc_debug_enabled; no parameters. Postcondition: static __init function returning int. It returns 0 with no other effect if mc_debug_enabled is false. Otherwise it allocates per-CPU debug data with alloc_percpu; if that fails it prints an error, decrements the mc_debug static key and returns -ENOMEM, with mc_debug_data_ptr unchanged. If it succeeds, it disables interrupts, calls xen_mc_flush, assigns the allocation to mc_debug_data_ptr, restores interrupts, prints an informational message and returns 0.
note: Checked multicalls.c:80-105. Prose was right; contract dropped because the function touches global state.

name: set_phys_to_machine
prose: Precondition: pfn and mfn are the frame numbers to map; the caller need not hold a lock. Postcondition: calls __set_phys_to_machine(pfn, mfn) and returns true if that returns true; that callee returns true after an atomic store into the p2m, for an entry that is the shared missing page with mfn equal to INVALID_P2M_ENTRY, for the identity page with mfn equal to IDENTITY_FRAME(pfn), and for pfn at or above xen_p2m_size when mfn is INVALID_P2M_ENTRY. If it returns false, set_phys_to_machine calls xen_alloc_p2m_entry(pfn); a negative result gives false, and otherwise it returns the result of a second __set_phys_to_machine(pfn, mfn). The p2m allocation can allocate p2m pages and update p2m_generation under p2m_update_lock; the caller gains no lock or reference.
note: Checked p2m.c:667-680, __set_phys_to_machine 639-665 and xen_alloc_p2m_entry 521-616. Reviewer round-15 claim that any pfn/mfn is not safe is PARTLY RIGHT: xen_alloc_p2m_entry has BUG_ON(!ptep || level != PG_LEVEL_4K) at 532 which could fire for a pfn outside the mapped p2m area; whether it does was not verified, so the precondition now claims nothing about arbitrary pfn. Round-2 claim right (second call result returned).

name: ATOMIC_OPS(add)
prose: Macro invocation that expands ATOMIC_OP, ATOMIC_FETCH_OP and ATOMIC_OP_RETURN for add, generating three inline functions on xtensa: arch_atomic_add(int i, atomic_t *v), arch_atomic_fetch_add(int i, atomic_t *v) and arch_atomic_add_return(int i, atomic_t *v). Precondition: v points to a valid atomic_t. Postcondition: each adds i to v->counter as a read-modify-write that retries or is interrupt-protected (an l32ex/s32ex loop when XCHAL_HAVE_EXCLUSIVE, an l32i/s32c1i compare-and-swap loop when XCHAL_HAVE_S32C1I, otherwise a sequence guarded by raising the interrupt level through rsil and restoring PS). Addition wraps on overflow. arch_atomic_add returns nothing; arch_atomic_fetch_add returns the value of the counter before the addition; arch_atomic_add_return returns the value after the addition.
note: Checked atomic.h:57-251. Reviewer round-15 claim RIGHT: macro expands to three functions, two of which return values. Name uses the macro invocation.

name: ATOMIC_OPS(sub)
prose: Macro invocation that expands ATOMIC_OP, ATOMIC_FETCH_OP and ATOMIC_OP_RETURN for sub, generating three inline functions on xtensa: arch_atomic_sub(int i, atomic_t *v), arch_atomic_fetch_sub(int i, atomic_t *v) and arch_atomic_sub_return(int i, atomic_t *v). Precondition: v points to a valid atomic_t.
